key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants must be designed as coupled biomechanical–biomaterial systems, where geometry, graded interfaces, and coating durability jointly control load transfer and osseointegration.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that patient-realistic finite element modeling and functionally graded Ti-HAp/surface-architecture design are central to improving distal support while limiting micromotion, stress peaks, and coating failure.
method: Systematic review of DWBI concepts, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation studies
Trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers plus 32 empirical studies
Synthesis of finite element gait-phase loading, FGMs, graded Ti-HAp, and in-vivo evidence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that more than half of the empirical evidence remained at the bench or simulation stage, with animal and clinical validation forming a smaller portion of the dataset.
watch_item: Graded Ti-HAp and FGM concepts are still supported mostly by non-DWBI analog studies, so device-level validation and coating-integrity testing remain necessary before clinical translation.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
